content: The University of California, Davis, commonly referred to as UC Davis, is one of the ten campuses of the University of California system. It was originally established in 1905 as the University Farm and later became a general UC campus in 1959. UC Davis is a public, coeducational university located in Davis, California, approximately 15 miles west of Sacramento in the Sacramento Valley, which is part of California's Central Valley. Over the years, UC Davis has evolved into a prestigious public research university, excelling in fields such as the arts, humanities, life sciences, health sciences, and engineering. UC Davis is home to several renowned graduate programs, including the UC Davis School of Medicine, which encompasses the UC Davis Medical Center, the UC Davis School of Veterinary Medicine, the UC Davis School of Law, and the UC Davis Graduate School of Management. In 2008, U.S. News & World Report ranked UC Davis as the 42nd best university in the United States, the 11th best public university in the nation, and the 4th best among the UC schools, following Berkeley, UCLA, and UC San Diego. It is also the third oldest campus in the UC system and is recognized as a Public Ivy institution. The university's athletic program is highly regarded, with the Aggie teams recently joining NCAA Division I athletics. UC Davis is one of only three UC schools with a football team, competing in the Great West Football Conference. The campus is also known for its vibrant and politically active student body, as well as its picturesque architecture and landscaping, which include broad green lawns, fountains, sculpture gardens, and a mix of architectural styles. The UC Davis campus spans two counties, Yolo and Solano, and is the only UC campus with its own airport. It also has its own fire department and a nuclear lab, shared only with UC Berkeley. The campus is surrounded by the residential area of the city of Davis and features extensive open spaces, including fields for various sports and recreational activities. The university library system, which includes the Peter J. Shields Library, the Physical Sciences & Engineering Library, the Carlson Health Sciences Library, and the Medical Center Library in Sacramento, houses over 3 million volumes and offers numerous special collections and services. The Shields Library, the main library on campus, is a large building with three distinct architectural styles due to various expansions. It serves as a central hub for student study and research, featuring a 24-hour reading room, computer labs, and unique furniture. The northeast end of the campus is home to the Quad, a large rectangular field adjacent to Freeborn Hall and the Memorial Union, which houses the UC Davis Bookstore, ASUCD Coffee House, food courts, a post office, and other facilities. The northwest end of the campus includes the Segundo undergraduate housing complex and other housing options such as Orchard Park and Russell Park. The Tercero housing complex is located near the geographic center of the campus, close to the Arboretum Waterway, which stretches across the southern end of the campus. UC Davis is also known for its public art, including the Egghead Series, a collection of five sculptures by former art professor Robert Arneson. These sculptures are considered iconic features of the campus and have inspired a university-maintained blog. Academically, UC Davis is strong in the arts, humanities, life sciences, health sciences, and engineering. It has a world-class medical center in downtown Sacramento and a Department of Viticulture and Enology that has made significant contributions to winemaking. The university is also noted for its programs in Agricultural and Resource Economics and Animal Science, offering students access to on-campus facilities such as a dairy, meat-processing plant, equestrian center, and experimental farm. The campus is home to the UC Davis Arboretum, which provides resources for students in environmental horticulture and botanical sciences. UC Davis has a distinguished faculty, including members of the National Academy of Sciences, the National Academy of Engineering, and the American Academy of Arts and Sciences, as well as Pulitzer Prize winners and MacArthur Fellows. The university supports numerous research centers and has been recognized for its contributions to ecology and evolution. Admissions to UC Davis are highly selective, with competitive SAT and ACT scores among admitted students. The university's athletic teams, known as the Aggies, compete in NCAA Division I sports, with notable achievements in football, basketball, and other sports. The Aggie Pack, the largest student-run school spirit organization in the United States, rallies students at sporting events. UC Davis is also famous for its annual Picnic Day, the largest student-run event in the country, featuring a parade, a chemistry magic show, dachshund races, film screenings, and a Battle of the Bands. The campus radio station, KDVS, has a rich history and is entirely student-run. The Associated Students of UC Davis (ASUCD) is the highest-funded student government in the United States, managing a budget of over $7 million. Greek life has been a part of UC Davis since 1923, with approximately 8% of undergraduates involved in fraternities and sororities. The university also has a strong focus on transportation, with a large number of bicycles and bike-friendly infrastructure. The student-run Unitrans bus service operates vintage London double-decker buses and provides transportation throughout the city. UC Davis is easily accessible by car, with two freeway exits entirely within its boundaries, and many students commute from nearby communities. In summary, UC Davis is a world-renowned institution known for its academic excellence, research contributions, vibrant student life, and unique campus features.
